title: What he did before Basie, and asking banjo and tuba men for help
summary: Jones says he tried dancing, singing and drama before drums and learned from banjo, tuba and guitar players, who told him whom to look up.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Your main thing is what you did before, your main gripe has always been that nobody talks about what you did before Basie. Now, what did you do before Basie?
Oh, Milt, I tried everything. I tried the dancing; I tried the singing; I tried the dramatics.
Then you did the same thing as Lionel Hampton, it seems.

Yeh, yeh. It's just like Lionel; he took all his eggs and put them in one basket. Now you must remember the peoples that I met that I had to ask that had been traveling places that I hadn't traveled to, and they would help me. The banjo players, the tuba players, the guitar players - not the drummers. I had never thought that I'd ever play drums. I never thought that I was going to be a Jimmy Bertrand. I didn't think like that. I would ask them; and then when I traveled around they'd tell me who to see. They'd say, 'Where are you going?' I'd say, 'I'm going so-and-so.' They'd say, 'Go look him up.'
This is what you in turn did when you became - famous as a drummer. You told the other guys.
Go look up so-and-so. Where are you going?
You going to Kansas City? Look up Baby Lovett. Look up Thigpen...
